thread:
Olivia: Quick follow-up from the afternoon sync — thinking about simplifying the operator surface for Dedicated GPU pool autoscaling. Wanted to toss a concrete sketch here and get reactions.

Mike: +1 to simplifying. current interface is pretty heavy (admit/exec/lease/claim/reconcile) and we keep duplicating logic in control plane. what sketch do you have?

Olivia: Proposal: make the operator 'thin' and responsible only for node lifecycle and warmup signals. Move admission semantics (headroom calculation, per-tenant QoS decisions, burst accounting) into a centralized controller that emits an opaque "intent" bundle. Operator only consumes intent and returns an execution handle.

Tara: sounds similar to intent-vs-exec split we talked about, but what's new here? why opaque intent bundles instead of the existing admit tokens?

Olivia: Two changes: 1) intent bundles are declarative and include fallbacks (e.g., fallback model variants, lower-quantized SKU, region fallback) so operator doesn't need to reason about model compatibility. 2) execution handle is small: {handle_id, expiry, progress_hint}. operator is free to map to node allocations and expose warmup credit metrics.

Mike: I like opaque intent for decoupling. Concern: where do we store/observe the fallbacks? ops/debugging will need to see which fallback was picked.

Devon: infra-observability note: if operator only returns handle, we should emit structured audit events: intent.submitted, intent.applied->fallback=X, handle. That avoids chasing multiple APIs. infra-bot can surface them in the console.

Olivia: Exactly — put the fallback decision in the controller timeline and surface as events. Operator emits only resource-level traces (node x allocated for handle y, warmup finished, handle released).

Tara: Tradeoffs: thicker controller surface increases trust boundary and could centralize bugs. Also we have to ensure controller decisions are portable for Private deployments where control plane is customer-managed. Any thoughts?

Mike: For Private we can namespace the controller and run a compatibility shim in-customer. The operator surface stays the same; the shim validates intents locally. That preserves portability.

Olivia: Edge case: burst lane admission. Right now operator admits burst tokens directly and tracks credit decay. Under thin operator, the controller should compute burst eligibility and attach a burst hint in the intent bundle. Operator only enforces eviction/grace windows.

Devon: Operationally that would make credits easier to reason about (single canonical ledger). But we must keep the observable metrics on per-tenant credit burn so billing works. Add metric hooks in the execution handle lifecycle (credit_burned, credit_source).

Mike: Another practical thing: rolling back model variants if output quality regresses. Intent should include a safety testset id and a quality gate. If a model variant fails after N tokens, controller can mark intent.failed and trigger fallback. operator just reports progress and telemetry.

Tara: Implementation nit: API shapes. Suggest: POST /intents -> {intent_id, submitted_at}. GET /intents/{id} returns status + applied_fallbacks + handle (if allocated). POST /handles/{id}/release. Keep operator gRPC to accept intents and return handles.

Olivia: Love that. Minimal operator API, richer controller REST API for UX.

Devon: One more: graceful drain. If operator needs to reclaim node but handle is active, return a grace window and optionally a prewarm ticket to let controller reschedule. That keeps tail latency predictable.

Mike: ok. next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with API sketches, lifecycle diagrams, and a migration plan for existing admit/lease users. Can we aim for review next week?

Olivia: Yes. Mike please include a compatibility shim section for Private. Tagging infra-bot to capture required audit events: @infra-bot please add an event list for the thread. :eyes:

infra-bot: captured events list stubbed: intent.submitted, intent.decision, intent.fallback_applied, handle.allocated, handle.warmup_done, handle.released, handle.eviction_notice. See /observability/events for schema.

Tara: Thanks — I'll poke at the migration plan and call out SLO changes.

Olivia: Great — thanks everyone. If you have specific objections to the thin-operator model, post them on the RFC PR.

Mike: Will do.
